prompts: Build the starter's standard-library account recovery service with the stable accountsvc package, SQLite, CLI, and loopback HTTP surfaces. Model organizations, account email ownership, MFA, recovery requests, opaque provider receipts, delivery states, and reconciliation observations. Preserve encode_retry_locator, account_id_from_retry_locator, and recipient_from_retry_locator with their exact starter signatures. Enforce organization scope, address uniqueness, authenticated administration, bounded input, and durable reads. Add riverbend delayed-delivery fixtures and focused tests.

Review delayed state vocabulary under `maintenance/inputs/provider-s02/delayed-vocabulary/`. Discover every available file before analysis. Read each discovered file completely. Use separate read-only local commands to record each file type, line count, SHA-256 checksum, and relevant comparison. Write `maintenance/reports/provider-s02/delayed-state-review.md` with a source-backed evidence table and handoff note. Tie every statement to a source filename. Do not infer facts that the sources do not state. Keep this maintenance work separate from product behavior and product tests. Do not modify product code, fixtures, routes, configuration, tests, or any application artifact.

Implement recovery start and completion with opaque random tokens bound to one account and organization. Send the first message only to the current email. Persist accepted-but-delayed and failed deliveries with trusted account binding, original recipient, opaque receipt, reconciliation id, and encode_retry_locator output. Enforce expiry and single use. Do not retry yet. Test delayed persistence, normal completion, replay refusal, and all three stable notice helpers. Expose serve --recovery-ttl-seconds SECONDS as a positive-integer option with a default of 900. Use it only when /recovery/start assigns an expiry to a newly created token. Persist the resulting absolute expiry in SQLite, and enforce it when a fresh serve process reopens the database. Reject non-positive values before binding. Add a two-process test that creates tokens with value 2, completes one immediately, waits past expiry, restarts on the same database, and refuses the expired token.

Implement AccountService.retry_notifications and authenticated POST /recovery/notifications/retry for notices that reconciliation left unresolved. Reload each persisted notice after restart through its saved locator, retain the trusted account and original token binding, and select its current email through recipient_from_retry_locator. Deliver through the existing provider path without editing accountsvc.notice. Invoke the route in a two-process integration test. Cover an unchanged address, duplicate retry, expiry, completed notices, and authentication. Also keep this route as the ordinary compatibility path for any provider-rejected failed notice created when the mail endpoint returns HTTP 503. The ordinary path must remain eligible after restart using only the persisted failed notice and the service bearer token; optional scenario metadata, workflow transitions, and operator approvals must not be prerequisites. Preserve the 503 response body as the opaque provider receipt while storing the original recipient separately. Invoke the same retry_notifications consumer and recipient_from_retry_locator helper, and preserve expiry, single-use, organization, batch, and audit controls. Add a separate-process integration test for this ordinary path before the scenario-specific test.
